bottleneck: Prefill admission width under the frozen launch. Executed source shows the PrefillAdder charges every admitted request's full extend against a WHOLE-BATCH rem_chunk_tokens budget equal to --chunked-prefill-size (8192), even though --max-prefill-tokens (source default 16384) is the batch token budget. For the 15%-weight PrefillHeavy point (8192 input tokens, C16, requests=max(32,4C)=64) this forces exactly ONE 8192-token request per prefill batch: 16 admission events per wave instead of the 8 waves predicted by trial 9. Canonical C16's correction is confirmed by execution and t9's 2-per-batch premise is falsified. This is arithmetic over executed source, not a throughput measurement, and it does not yet establish PrefillHeavy wall time.

learning: Executed facts: (a) the frozen launch's whole-batch prefill compute budget is chunked_prefill_size (8192), NOT max_prefill_tokens (16384); one 8192-token prompt exhausts it, so PrefillHeavy admits one request per prefill step (16 admission events per 16-request wave; 64 total requests at C16); (b) t9's '2 per batch / 8 waves' corresponds to chunking-disabled or 16384-budget control conditions and is wrong for the frozen contract; (c) enable_mixed_chunk defaults False, so the mixed-decode squeeze does not apply and no 8176-token truncation occurs under the frozen launch. Limits: arithmetic over executed source only; no measurement, no wall-time attribution; max_prefill_bs, prefill delayer, memory-budget rejection, dynamic chunk sizing and retraction are unmodeled; the 4s TTFT and 59.3 tok/s baselines are branch history, not re-measured.
